Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:08:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy fires on two distinct error classes visible in the proxy's own spans and Envoy access logs. (1) The dominant class is POST /api/checkout returning 504 with Envoy flags 'UT response_timeout' at the 15 s route timeout, sent upstream to frontend. frontend's own /api/checkout span completes with http.status_code 200 only after 47.9-91.4 s, because checkout's 'orders publish' span (Kafka produce) errors for 100% of PlaceOrder calls with 'circuit breaker is open' / 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker' and takes 45-91 s. The Kafka brokers themselves log a continuous StaleBrokerEpochException loop and a conflicting broker epoch for broker/node id 1, while the kafka Deployment runs 2 replicas against a config that declares a single-voter KRaft quorum 1@kafka:9093, advertises PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092 (a Service that load-balances over both pods) and has no per-pod node id; both pods' logs identify themselves as node id 1. That configuration is the deepest cause the evidence supports. (2) A second class appeared later: GET /api/data returning 500 (21 ms, via_upstream) matching frontend's own ERROR spans on 'GET /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds'; the ad container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 18:26:22 and restarted once, but ad's own server spans show no ERROR status and ad logs show it serving requests, so the exact ad-side mechanism is unresolved. Chaos Mesh PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events target checkout and both kafka pods from 18:28:10 to 18:36:10, coinciding with the error peak; since the first 504s and Kafka epoch errors precede the earliest visible chaos event, the chaos is recorded as an unresolved candidate, not the established cause. Affected with own evidence: frontend-proxy (own error spans, 504/500 responses), checkout (own failing publish spans and 'circuit breaker is open' logs), kafka (own broker-epoch/assignment errors), frontend (own ERROR spans) and ad (OOMKilled exit 137). Checked and not shown to be failing: cart, payment, currency and product-catalog returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in the sampled checkout traces, and all 22 otel-demo pods were Running/ready; this is not a full health clearance of those services. Changed during the window with undetermined cause: every otel-demo pod was created at 17:56:42-44 (full redeploy) before the first observed errors; change history is not integrated, so this is a gap, not impact.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span metrics expose two span names: 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), each with STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET series.

The 5-minute error rate of frontend-proxy spans rose inside the visible window: ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.18/s at 18:09:41 to a peak of ~1.24/s at 18:32-18:37 and 0.148/s at 18:42:41; 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 until ~18:22:41, peaked at 0.77/s at 18:32-18:37 and returned to 0 by 18:42:41.

frontend-proxy Envoy access logs at 18:09:44-18:09:58 show repeated '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000/15001 ... frontend' entries, i.e. upstream response timeouts at 15 s against the frontend cluster.

frontend-proxy Envoy access logs at 18:36:22-18:37:16 still show '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' at 15000-15001 ms upstream 'frontend', while /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products and /api/recommendations returned 200 in the same interval.

In a sampled trace at ~18:09:26, frontend-proxy ingress spans ended in error with http.status_code 504 after ~15.0008 s, their child 'router frontend egress' spans lasted ~15.0006 s with http.status_code 0, while the same trace's frontend 'POST /api/checkout' span lasted 47.93 s and returned http.status_code 200, and checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' lasted 47.93 s with its child 'orders publish' span taking 47.40 s and ending with otel.status_description 'circuit breaker is open'.

In sampled traces at 18:24-18:25, frontend-proxy ingress spans are 15.0 s 504s and checkout 'orders publish' spans lasting 87-91 s carry error details 'circuit breaker is open' and 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker'; the matching frontend 'POST /api/checkout' spans last 91.1-91.4 s.

checkout's 'orders publish' STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase equals the 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' span count in every observed 10-minute bucket (257.8 vs 257.8 at 18:18:41, 247.4 vs 247.4 at 18:28:41, 270.5 vs 270.5 at 18:38:41), so every observed PlaceOrder carried a failing publish span.

checkout container logs at 18:36:08-18:36:49 contain 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', 'kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: circuit breaker is open', 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout' and 'client/brokers deregistered broker #1 at kafka:9092'.

kafka-ff7884766-xclnk logs every ~10 s from 18:07:59 to 18:09:59 include '[QuorumController id=1] assignReplicasToDirs: event failed with StaleBrokerEpochException ... Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10', '[ControllerApis nodeId=1] Unexpected error handling request ... AssignReplicasToDirsRequestData(brokerId=1, brokerEpoch=10, ... topicId=mLbHo9e8TDqsEg5P-1AJgA partitions 0-49 ...)' and '[NodeToControllerChannelManager id=1 name=registration] Node 1 disconnected.'

kafka-ff7884766-skk8d logs every ~10 s from 18:12:38 to 18:22:25 contain '[AssignmentsManager id=1] handleResponse: 50 assignments failed; global error: Response-level error: STALE_BROKER_EPOCH. Retrying.'

Deployment kafka in otel-demo has spec.replicas 2 and 2 ready replicas, with container env KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093, KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER and KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093, and no per-pod node-id variable.
ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 is owned by Deployment kafka, has deployment revision 1, was created 2026-11-16T17:56:42Z and runs spec.replicas 2 with 2 ready replicas.
The kafka Service endpoints include both broker pods: 100.96.2.21 -> kafka-ff7884766-skk8d and 100.96.4.61 -> kafka-ff7884766-xclnk, so 'kafka:9092' load-balances across both brokers.
Both kafka pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 (created 17:56:43), and all 22 pods in otel-demo were Running/ready at query time, with ad the only pod showing a restart (1).

Kubernetes events of involvedObject kind PodNetworkChaos with reason 'Updated' reference checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l, kafka-ff7884766-skk8d and kafka-ff7884766-xclnk between 18:28:10Z and 18:36:10Z, about once per pod per minute.

Ingress ERROR span durations differ by period: in 18:07:42-18:17:42 there were 306.2 error spans of which only ~3 were within 15 s (303 above 15 s); in 18:28:41-18:38:41 there were 593.7 error spans, with 193.7 at <=4 ms, 214.7 at <=50 ms and 258.9 at <=15 s.
frontend-proxy Envoy access logs show 'GET /api/data...' returning 500 via_upstream with 21 ms total and 2-3 ms upstream time at 18:30:39-18:30:59 and again at 18:33:40-18:33:54.

frontend's own 'GET /api/data' STATUS_CODE_ERROR count rose 0 -> 70.5 -> 253.7 per 10 minutes and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' STATUS_CODE_ERROR matched it exactly, while ad's server-side 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans appear only as STATUS_CODE_UNSET (388.9, 357.9, 183.1 per 10 minutes).

The ad container's last termination was reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-16T18:26:22Z (restartCount 1); the ad Deployment sets memory limit 450Mi and CPU limit 50m, and ad container Started events occur at 17:56:45 and 18:26:22.
ad container logs at 18:36:58-18:37:15 show normal request handling ('Targeted ad request received for [binoculars]', 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.').

All otel-demo pods were created at 17:56:42-17:56:44Z (including frontend-proxy, checkout, both kafka pods and otel-collector), and span-metric series for these services only have samples from about 18:07 onward, so no pre-incident error baseline is available.

Primary cause: the otel-demo kafka Deployment runs 2 broker replicas against single-node KRaft settings (quorum voters 1@kafka:9093, advertised listener via the load-balancing kafka:9092 Service, no per-pod node id), and both pods log themselves as node id 1 in a continuous StaleBrokerEpochException / 'Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' loop; the resulting loss of valid partition leadership makes checkout's produce to topic 'orders' fail or hang, which stretches PlaceOrder to 45-91 s, exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout and produces the 504 UT /api/checkout responses that drive frontend-proxy's error rate.

Second, independent error source: the fast (~21 ms) frontend-proxy 500 responses on GET /api/data correspond to frontend's failing ad path (frontend ERROR spans on 'GET /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', 0 -> 70.5 -> 253.7 per 10 min) around the ad container's OOMKill at 18:26:22 (exit 137); this class added roughly 194 error spans in 18:28-18:38 and is separate from the kafka-driven /api/checkout 504s.

Unresolved candidate cause: Chaos Mesh network fault injection on checkout and both kafka pods (PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events 18:28:10-18:36:10) overlaps the 18:28-18:38 error peak; however the earliest observed /api/checkout 504s (18:09) and Kafka epoch errors (18:07:59) precede the earliest visible chaos event, so it is not established as the trigger and cannot be verified as the cause of the peak.

Pod-level status does not show the Kafka fault: the kafka Deployment is fully available (2/2 ready) and both broker pods are Running with restartCount 0, so kafka being 'healthy' cannot be concluded from pod phase/readiness.

ad-side evidence does not show ad returning errors: ad's own 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR series), and ad logs at 18:36-18:37 show it serving requests, so the /api/data 500s are visible only on frontend's client spans and the proxy's responses.

The /api/checkout 504s are not a frontend 5xx: Envoy flags them 'UT response_timeout' at its own 15 s route timeout, and the corresponding frontend server spans complete with http.status_code 200 after 47.9-91.4 s, i.e. a slow-but-eventually-successful upstream path.

Rejected: 'frontend-proxy itself is the faulty component / frontend is returning 5xx'. The proxy's 504s are its own 15 s upstream timeouts to the 'frontend' cluster while other frontend routes returned 200, and frontend's checkout spans ended with http.status_code 200 at 47.9-91.4 s; the fault lies below frontend in checkout's Kafka produce path.

Rejected: 'the kafka brokers crashed or were OOMKilled/Evicted'. Both kafka pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and show no Evicted or OOMKilled marks; their failure is a runtime broker-epoch/assignment conflict (StaleBrokerEpochException), not a container crash.

Fix the kafka topology: either run the kafka Deployment as a single broker (matching KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 and the single node id in the image) or give each replica a unique node id, per-pod advertised listener and per-pod DNS, then verify that topic 'orders' partitions have leaders before declaring recovery.

Separately review the ad workload: investigate why the ad container exceeded its 450Mi memory limit (OOMKilled exit 137 at 18:26:22) and collect frontend error details for the failing AdService/GetAds calls that surface as GET /api/data 500s.

Locate the Alertmanager rule source for RequestErrorRate (it is not present in the queried Prometheus) to confirm the exact expression and threshold behind the reported value 1.6, and check the Chaos Mesh experiment schedule for network faults on the kafka and checkout pods.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not found in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression, labels and the reported value 1.6 could not be verified against a metric series.

Change history is not integrated, so whether kafka's 2-replica configuration (or a chaos experiment) was introduced at the 17:56:42 pod recreation cannot be established; all 22 otel-demo pods were created 17:56:42-44 and no earlier object state is observable.

Span-metric series for these services start around 18:07, so no pre-incident error-rate or latency baseline exists to quantify how far the 18:08-18:42 error rate exceeds normal for frontend-proxy /api/checkout.
Kafka pod logs before ~18:12 could not be read (4 MiB log read limit reached), so the first occurrence of the StaleBrokerEpoch loop relative to the 17:56 broker start is unknown.

Chaos resources themselves (NetworkChaos objects) are not among the readable Kubernetes kinds; only PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events from 18:28:10-18:36:10 were observed, so whether a network fault was active earlier and whether it contributed to the 18:28-18:38 peak is unknown.

The mechanism of the GET /api/data 500s is unresolved: the frontend pod produced no readable log lines, Jaeger returned no traces for frontend/frontend-proxy after about 18:26, and ad's own spans show no ERROR status; only frontend's client-side ERROR spans and the proxy's 500 responses document it.

No kafka ConfigMap exists in otel-demo, so the brokers' node.id/quorum settings come from the container image and could not be read directly; the duplicate node-id conclusion rests on both pods' log lines (xclnk 'ControllerApis nodeId=1' / 'brokerId=1', skk8d 'AssignmentsManager id=1').

Services accounting, email, fraud-detection, image-provider, quote, recommendation, shipping, currency, payment, cart, product-catalog, valkey-cart, postgresql and flagd were not individually error-checked; only their pod phase/readiness and rpc.grpc.status_code 0 on some sampled checkout calls were observed, so they are neither cleared nor shown affected.
next_steps: Review the kafka Deployment spec and its history: confirm whether replicas=2 with KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 and a fixed node id is intended; remediate by scaling to one broker or by giving each broker a distinct node id, advertised listener and per-pod DNS.
Verify the Kafka cluster state (topic 'orders', 50 partitions, partition leaders/ISR) once brokers are stable, and confirm checkout produce failures clear.
Retrieve the Alertmanager RequestErrorRate rule definition from its source to confirm which metric/threshold produced the 1.6 value.
Inspect scheduled Chaos Mesh experiments covering 18:07-18:38 for network faults on kafka and checkout pods.
Investigate the ad container OOM (450Mi limit, exit 137 at 18:26:22) and capture frontend error detail for the failing AdService/GetAds calls behind the /api/data 500s.

Unresolved candidate cause: Chaos Mesh network fault injection on checkout and both kafka pods (PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events 18:28:10-18:36:10) overlaps the 18:28-18:38 error peak; however the earliest observed /api/checkout 504s (18:09) and Kafka epoch errors (18:07:59) precede the earliest visible chaos event, so it is not established as the trigger and cannot be verified as the cause of the peak.

recommendation.text: Fix the kafka topology: either run the kafka Deployment as a single broker (matching KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 and the single node id in the image) or give each replica a unique node id, per-pod advertised listener and per-pod DNS, then verify that topic 'orders' partitions have leaders before declaring recovery.

Separately review the ad workload: investigate why the ad container exceeded its 450Mi memory limit (OOMKilled exit 137 at 18:26:22) and collect frontend error details for the failing AdService/GetAds calls that surface as GET /api/data 500s.

Locate the Alertmanager rule source for RequestErrorRate (it is not present in the queried Prometheus) to confirm the exact expression and threshold behind the reported value 1.6, and check the Chaos Mesh experiment schedule for network faults on the kafka and checkout pods.

counter_evidence.text: Pod-level status does not show the Kafka fault: the kafka Deployment is fully available (2/2 ready) and both broker pods are Running with restartCount 0, so kafka being 'healthy' cannot be concluded from pod phase/readiness.

ad-side evidence does not show ad returning errors: ad's own 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR series), and ad logs at 18:36-18:37 show it serving requests, so the /api/data 500s are visible only on frontend's client spans and the proxy's responses.

The /api/checkout 504s are not a frontend 5xx: Envoy flags them 'UT response_timeout' at its own 15 s route timeout, and the corresponding frontend server spans complete with http.status_code 200 after 47.9-91.4 s, i.e. a slow-but-eventually-successful upstream path.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: 'frontend-proxy itself is the faulty component / frontend is returning 5xx'. The proxy's 504s are its own 15 s upstream timeouts to the 'frontend' cluster while other frontend routes returned 200, and frontend's checkout spans ended with http.status_code 200 at 47.9-91.4 s; the fault lies below frontend in checkout's Kafka produce path.

Rejected: 'the kafka brokers crashed or were OOMKilled/Evicted'. Both kafka pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and show no Evicted or OOMKilled marks; their failure is a runtime broker-epoch/assignment conflict (StaleBrokerEpochException), not a container crash.
